_about: Every country with homes on RealHunt: key figures, buying costs and the rule for foreign buyers
note: Asking prices in euros from the original listing on the day each home was added. Medians describe the homes RealHunt lists (cheap for their country, checked by a person), not a country's whole market. Rules, taxes and costs are general information, not legal or tax advice.

countries.can_foreigners_buy: Yes. Foreigners can buy property in France without major restrictions, and non-EU buyers do not need a permit, although the paperwork can take longer.
countries.annual_property_tax: Owners pay an annual property tax (taxe foncière) set by the local authorities, and owners of a furnished second home also pay housing tax (taxe d'habitation), which some communes raise by a surcharge of 5% to 60%.

countries.can_foreigners_buy: Yes, no restrictions at present; the government has proposed a 100% tax on (or ban for) non-EU non-resident buyers, not enacted.
countries.annual_property_tax: IBI 0.4-1.1% of cadastral value (municipal), plus imputed income tax on unlet homes.

countries.can_foreigners_buy: Yes for EU citizens; non-EU buyers need reciprocity (US, UK, Canada, Australia qualify).
countries.annual_property_tax: IMU 0.4-1.06% on second homes (on cadastral value).

countries.can_foreigners_buy: Yes. Buyers from outside the EU and EFTA need a permit to buy in designated border areas (parts of northern Greece and eastern Aegean islands such as the Dodecanese and Rhodes). The government has announced a 15% transfer tax for non-EU buyers of homes from 1 January 2027, not yet final in September 2026.
countries.annual_property_tax: Owners on 1 January pay the unified property tax (ENFIA), calculated per property from its location, size, age and official zone value, with an extra charge if total Greek property exceeds €500,000.

countries.can_foreigners_buy: Yes. There is no federal ban on foreigners buying homes, but about 30 states have added some limits, and Texas and Florida restrict buyers from certain countries such as China.
countries.annual_property_tax: Property tax is set locally and in 2024 averaged about 1.22% of value across the largest city in each state, from 0.30% in Honolulu to 3.02% in Detroit.

countries.can_foreigners_buy: Without Danish domicile or 5 years of past residence you need permission from the Department of Civil Affairs (Civilstyrelsen); EU/EEA citizens who live and are registered in Denmark can buy a permanent home without permission by signing a declaration to the Land Registration Court. Holiday homes (sommerhuse) need permission, which is only given to people with particularly strong ties to Denmark, such as many years of holidays there.
countries.annual_property_tax: Owners pay property value tax (ejendomsværdiskat) of 0.51% on 80% of the official valuation (1.4% above DKK 9.2 million) plus municipal land tax (grundskyld) at a rate set by each municipality, capped at 30 per mille of the land value.

countries.can_foreigners_buy: Yes, same rights as Portuguese citizens (IMT increase for foreign second-home buyers announced Sept 2025).
countries.annual_property_tax: IMI 0.3-0.45% of taxable value (urban), set by municipality.

countries.can_foreigners_buy: Yes. There are no citizenship or residence rules for buying a home in Sweden, but you need a Swedish personal identity number or coordination number (samordningsnummer) to register ownership.
countries.annual_property_tax: Houses pay a municipal property fee (kommunal fastighetsavgift) of SEK 10,425 in 2026, or 0.75% of the tax value if that is lower.

countries.can_foreigners_buy: EU, EEA and Swiss citizens buy on the same terms as Poles. Other foreigners can buy an apartment without a permit, but usually need a permit from the Ministry of the Interior (MSWiA) to buy a house or land.
countries.annual_property_tax: Owners pay a local property tax (podatek od nieruchomości) set by the commune, capped in 2026 at PLN 1.25 per m² of usable floor space for flats and houses.

countries.can_foreigners_buy: Yes. Foreigners can buy freehold land and homes on the same terms as Japanese citizens, even on a tourist visa, though buying does not give a visa or residency.
countries.annual_property_tax: Fixed asset tax is 1.4% of the government's assessed value, plus city planning tax of up to 0.3% in urban areas, and small residential plots get a lower tax base.

countries.can_foreigners_buy: Mostly not for now: a federal ban stops non-Canadians from buying homes in cities and larger towns until January 1, 2027, with exceptions such as work permit holders and spouses of citizens or permanent residents. The ban does not cover rural areas and small towns, and the government has said it does not plan simply to extend it, but a replacement is being studied.
countries.annual_property_tax: Property tax is set by each city as a share of assessed value, from about 0.3% in Vancouver to 2.12% in Saint John in 2026.

countries.can_foreigners_buy: Yes. There are no restrictions on foreigners buying property in Germany, though non-EU buyers usually need a bigger down payment to get a loan.
countries.annual_property_tax: Owners pay property tax (Grundsteuer), calculated since 2025 as assessed value x a tax rate x a municipal multiplier (Hebesatz) that each municipality sets.

countries.can_foreigners_buy: Yes. There are no nationality or residence rules and no surcharge for foreign buyers. Some cities, such as The Hague, restrict renting out cheaper homes after purchase without a permit (opkoopbescherming).
countries.annual_property_tax: Owners pay municipal property tax (onroerendezaakbelasting, OZB) on the official WOZ value, at a rate each municipality sets, which in practice is a per mille figure; tenants of homes do not pay it.

countries.can_foreigners_buy: Yes, but in the Restricted Zone (within 50 km of the coast or 100 km of borders, which covers Tulum and Playa del Carmen) only through a fideicomiso bank trust or a Mexican company; direct ownership elsewhere.
countries.annual_property_tax: Municipal predial, set locally on cadastral value; usually small, often less than HOA fees.

countries.can_foreigners_buy: Under the Lex Koller law, EU/EFTA citizens living in Switzerland and holders of a C permit buy like Swiss citizens, and non-EU holders of a B permit can buy a home they live in. People living abroad need a cantonal permit and can usually only buy one holiday home in a tourist area, within national quotas; a proposed tightening was under consultation in 2026.
countries.annual_property_tax: More than half of the cantons charge an annual property tax (Liegenschaftssteuer), usually 0.01-0.3% of the assessed value, and owners also pay cantonal wealth tax on the property value minus the mortgage.

countries.can_foreigners_buy: Yes, buildings and apartments, with rights similar to locals; per GPG, foreigners can't own land directly, so a Bulgarian company is the usual route.
countries.annual_property_tax: 0.01-0.45% of the property's tax value plus a municipal garbage fee.

countries.can_foreigners_buy: Yes. There are no nationality restrictions on buying homes anywhere in the UK and no visa is needed, but buying does not give a right to live there.
countries.annual_property_tax: Owners or occupiers pay council tax to the local council, and many councils in England charge second homes a premium of up to 100% from April 2025.

countries.can_foreigners_buy: Yes. There are no limits on the types of property foreign buyers can purchase in Uruguay, and they have the same property rights as citizens.

EU citizens buy without restrictions. Non-EU buyers need permission from the Council of Ministers, applied for through the District Officer, and are normally limited to one home or a plot of up to 4,014 m².
countries.annual_property_tax: There is no annual national property tax (abolished in 2017); owners pay municipal fees of about €90 to €300 a year, plus sewerage and local authority charges.

countries.can_foreigners_buy: Yes. Foreigners have the same rights as Dominican citizens to buy land and homes, with no restrictions.
countries.annual_property_tax: The yearly IPI tax is 1% of the part of a person's total Dominican property value, as assessed by the tax office DGII, above RD$10,695,494 in 2026, so a single cheap home is often below the threshold.

countries.can_foreigners_buy: Yes. There are no restrictions on foreigners buying homes in Ireland, and owning a home does not give a right to live there.
countries.annual_property_tax: Local Property Tax (LPT): from 2026 a home valued up to €240,000 pays a basic €95 a year and one valued €240,001 to €315,000 pays €235; each council can raise or lower the basic rate by up to 15%, and most raised it by 15% for 2026.

countries.can_foreigners_buy: Yes. A home bought by a foreigner counts as foreign investment, which needs no prior authorization and is treated the same as investment by residents. When the money comes in through the foreign exchange market, the exchange declaration serves as its registration with the Banco de la República.
countries.annual_property_tax: Impuesto predial unificado: each municipality sets the rate between 5 and 16 per thousand of the cadastral value (avalúo catastral).

countries.can_foreigners_buy: Yes. Foreigners can buy homes and land in the Czech Republic on the same terms as Czechs: the limits on homes ended on 1 May 2009 and those on farmland and forest on 1 May 2011.
countries.annual_property_tax: Owners pay a yearly tax on land and buildings (daň z nemovitých věcí); from 2024 the rates rose to 1.8 times their old level on average, and each municipality can multiply the tax by a local coefficient between 0.5 and 5. The return is due by 31 January and the tax by 31 May.

countries.can_foreigners_buy: Yes for citizens of EU, EEA and OECD countries (such as the United States, the United Kingdom and Canada), who buy like Slovenians. Citizens of EU candidate countries (North Macedonia, Serbia, Montenegro, Albania, Ukraine, Moldova, Bosnia and Herzegovina and Georgia) first need a decision confirming reciprocity, and citizens of other countries, such as China and Russia, cannot buy, only inherit where reciprocity exists.
countries.annual_property_tax: The direct user of the home, usually the owner, pays a yearly fee for the use of building land (nadomestilo za uporabo stavbnega zemljišča, NUSZ), set by each municipality's ordinance and assessed once a year by the tax administration (FURS); owners of holiday homes also pay property tax (davek od premoženja).
